summary: Alfred Cort Haddon studied at King's College London (~1871–1872) and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1875–1879). He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1879–1880, 1900–1926) and the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901).
Working in Indology and linguistics, Alfred Darby studied at St Augustine's College, Canterbury, and Durham University (B.D. by 1908). He held a post at Rajaram College.

Alfred Edward Housman worked in linguistics and other fields. After attending King Edward's School, Bromsgrove School, and St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881), he held a post at University College London (~1892–1911).

Linguist Alfred Ernout studied at Lille, EPHE, and the Sorbonne under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at Lycée de Troyes, University of Lille (1913–1924), EPHE (from 1925), University of Paris (from 1924), and Collège de France (1944–1951).

Sinologist and philosopher Alfred Forke studied at Geneva, Berlin, Rostock, and under Carl Arendt at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen. He held professorships at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1903–1923), UC Berkeley (1914–1918), and Hamburg (1923–1935).

Alfred Foucher worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at ENS and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, later serving at the University of Paris (1907, 1929–1936) and directing the Délégation Archéologique Française en Afghanistan (1922–1925).

Alfred Gell studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, under Edmund Leach, and earned his Ph.D. at the LSE. He held academic posts at the University of Sussex (1972–1974), Australian National University (1974–1979), and the LSE (1979–1997).

Indologist and linguist Alfred Hillebrandt studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Martin Haug. He spent his career at the University of Breslau, serving as professor from 1887 to 1921.
Alfred Horsford Bingley was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who was educated at Kensington School and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (~1884–1885).

Historian, archaeologist, and linguist Alfred Körte studied at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890). He held posts at the universities of Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig (~1917–1934).
Indologist Alfred Louis Noël de Sadous studied under Eugène Burnouf and earned his doctorate at the University of Paris by 1847. He held a teaching post at Lycée Hoche.

Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied in Vienna and Berlin under Anton Boller, Hermann Bonitz, August Boeckh, Moriz Haupt, Albrecht Weber, and Friedrich Müller. He held professorships in classical philology and comparative linguistics at Charles University (1860–1901).

Indologist and linguist Alfred Master studied at Epsom College and the University of Oxford. He taught Gujarati and Indian philology at SOAS (1937–1939, 1944–1950) and served as Assistant Keeper at the India Office Records (1951–1957).

Philosopher Alfred North Whitehead was educated at Sherborne School and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1884–1910), Imperial College London (1914–1924), and Harvard University (1924–1937).

Alfred Nottrott was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Halle (1860) and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. by 1887). He served as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church from 1867.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, under W. H. R. Rivers. He held academic appointments at the University of Sydney (~1926–1931), University of Chicago (~1931–1937), Oxford (~1937–1946), and FESP in São Paulo (~1942–1944).

Specializing in Indology and religious studies, Alfred Roussel studied under Abel Bergaigne and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault after attending Saint-Malo and Rennes seminaries. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Fribourg (1903–1920).

Linguist Alfred Schmitt studied at Gnadenfeld Theological Seminary and the University of Rostock under Gustav Herbig and Hermann Güntert. He taught at the universities of Rostock (1928–1935), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1935–1941), and Münster (1941–1956).

Scholarly active in religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Alfred Shenington Geden studied at Oxford and Aberdeen. He served as Principal of Royapettah College (1886–1889) and taught at Richmond College (~1891–1920) and Wesleyan College (1891–1915).

Indologist and linguist Alfred William Stratton studied at the University of Toronto and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield. He held posts at the University of Chicago (1895–1899), Oriental College (1899), and the University of the Punjab (~1899–1902).
